name: Indian Coffee House (Statue Junction)
signature_dish: Filter coffee and masala dosa inside Laurie Baker's spiral building
why_it_matters: The most architecturally famous Indian Coffee House in India — a spiralling brick drum designed by architect Laurie Baker around 1989-90, where each table sits a step above the last as the ramp winds around the central kitchen. The jali brickwork and exposed-brick walls are a landmark of Baker's neo-vernacular style; the cooperative serves the same unchanging cheap menu inside.
insider_tip: Worth visiting as much for the building as the food — climb the spiral ramp for a table near the top. Order filter coffee and the mutton cutlet. Cash preferred; expect it busy and a little worn.
signature_address: Indian Coffee House, Statue Junction, MG Road, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala 695001

name: Villa Maya
signature_dish: Spice-route fusion menu blending Kerala with Mediterranean and Moroccan flavours
why_it_matters: Trivandrum's premier fine-dining restaurant, set in a restored 18th-century Dutch manor that once enjoyed the patronage of the Travancore royal house. The menu is a spice-route fusion — Kerala blended with Greek, Moroccan and Italian influences — served in antique-furnished rooms, stone-roof courtyard gazebos or a statue-and-fountain garden.
insider_tip: The most special-occasion restaurant in the city — reserve, and ask for a courtyard gazebo or garden table. It is genuinely fine dining, priced accordingly. Enter through the stone archway off Airport Road.
signature_address: Villa Maya, Airport Road, Injakkal, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala 695024

name: Hotel Rahmaniya (Kethel's Chicken)
signature_dish: Kethel's chicken fry — the patented secret-spice fried chicken
why_it_matters: A Chalai Bazaar institution started in the late 1940s by Muhammed Abdul Khader — 'Kethel Sahib' — and serving its famous Kethel's chicken fry for more than 70 years. The fried chicken, made with a patented secret blend of Kerala spices, is the dish Trivandrum locals send visitors to Chalai for; the brand has since grown to six restaurants across Kerala.
insider_tip: Go to the original in Chalai Bazaar and order the Kethel's chicken fry — that is the dish, full stop. It pairs well with Kerala porotta. Busy bazaar location; cash and UPI.
signature_address: Hotel Rahmaniya, Chalai Bazaar, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala 695036

name: Mothers Veg Plaza
signature_dish: Kerala sadya served on banana leaf 365 days a year, plus 100-plus dosa varieties
why_it_matters: One of Trivandrum's best-known pure-vegetarian restaurants, near Bakery Junction in Palayam. Its standout claim is serving the full Kerala sadya — a 26-item banana-leaf feast — every single day, not just at Onam, alongside more than 100 dosa varieties from the classic to the novelty Jini and chocolate dosa.
insider_tip: Take a coupon (around ₹250 for the sadya) first, then find a seat. It gets crowded and hectic at lunch — go a little early. For the full Kerala vegetarian experience, order the sadya.
signature_address: Mothers Veg Plaza, near Bakery Junction, Palayam, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala 695034

name: Buhari Hotel
signature_dish: Budget mutton biryani served 24 hours, with the local 'biryani chai'
why_it_matters: A 24-hour biryani house at Attakulangara in East Fort, long known among Trivandrum locals for cheap mutton biryani. Reviewers single out its 'biryani chai' — a local quirk worth trying — and the low price point that keeps it busy round the clock near the East Fort and Padmanabhaswamy Temple area.
insider_tip: Open 24 hours, so it is the go-to for a late-night or early-morning biryani. It is a basic, no-frills room — hygiene can be patchy; go for the freshly cooked biryani at peak hours. Cash and UPI.
signature_address: Buhari Hotel, Attakulangara, East Fort, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala 695023

name: Swathi at Mascot Hotel (KTDC)
signature_dish: Kerala meals and multi-cuisine dishes at the state tourism heritage hotel
why_it_matters: Swathi is the restaurant of the Mascot Hotel — a heritage property at Mascot Square in Palayam run by KTDC, the Kerala state tourism corporation. The building was originally put up to house Royal British Army officers in World War I; it is the only heritage business hotel in Trivandrum. Swathi is a comfortable, dependable city-centre option for Kerala meals and multi-cuisine fare.
insider_tip: A reliable central choice when you want an air-conditioned hotel restaurant rather than a street-side place — lunch is usually a buffet, dinner a la carte. Non-residents are welcome; call ahead at busy times.
signature_address: Swathi, Mascot Hotel, Mascot Square, Palayam, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala 695033
